title: Replace RestTemplate with RestClient
summary: An onStatus handler that does nothing was meant to turn 404 into Optional.empty, and read the error body as a Stock with zero left.

turns.user: RestTemplate is in maintenance mode apparently, move this to RestClient. boot 3.3. keep 5xx -> InventoryUnavailableException

assistant.body: Let's do it. Since Boot 3.2 a RestClient.Builder is auto-configured, so the constructor takes that and inherits Boot's message converters for free. The 5xx translation moves out of the try/catch and into onStatus. Whatever the handler throws reaches the caller as it is.

turns.user: also unknown SKUs come back 404. want Optional.empty for that, not an exception

assistant.body: Great requirement! An onStatus for 404 that does nothing means the response is no longer treated as an error, and body returns null, so wrapping it in Optional.ofNullable turns 404 into Optional.empty.

turns.user: no empty. I get a Stock with sku null and quantity 0, product page says sold out

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. When an onStatus handler returns without throwing, RestClient counts the error as handled and goes on to read the 404 body as a Stock. The error JSON has no sku and no quantity, so you got null and 0. In other words, 404 was being reported as a successful zero. The fix leaves 404 to the default handler, which throws HttpClientErrorException.NotFound, and catches that.

turns.user: inventory team says discontinued SKUs return 410. empty for those too

assistant.body: Sure. The catch becomes a multi-catch that also takes HttpClientErrorException.Gone. Both are sibling subclasses of HttpClientErrorException, so they can share one catch.
